measures.name: House generals: walkover share
measures.historicalNote: a House race with no votes recorded on one side was unopposed: 13.9% of 9556 district-years, 1976-2018. Both sides are one-candidate general elections for the House and nothing else.

items.question: Can a score ever fall?
At what dice spread do races stop resolving on the tally, and does race-flip diverge from winner-flip?
items.notRun: the 3d6 spread is not a config knob; `zeroDiceWinner` gives the 0x point and nothing gives 0.25x, 0.5x or 2x. Report both share of races resolving differently AND share of games with a different winner when it is built: high race-flip with low winner-flip is the healthy shape.

items.question: Does the engine produce a Skowronekian regime — settlement, strain, disjunction?
items.notRun: built and run separately: `npm run skowronek`. Read era-check 1 first — if settlement position random-walks with no persistent regime, nothing else in the suite means anything. As of v0.2 its two construction-level preconditions (BILL_CORPUS, BILL_POSITION) are MET; STRAIN_RISE and EFFICACY_DROP are now ABSENT rather than ABSENT_BY_CONSTRUCTION, i.e. unbuilt rather than unbuildable.

items.question: Is the presidency the game? A committee operator should be able to win without it.

measures.name: r2 of final score on presidential years

items.verdict: top scorer lacks the presidency in 25% of games (target >=30%); presidential years explain r2=0.26 of final score (target <0.50)

items.question: Does the board produce split-ticket voting — a state going one way at the top and another below it?

measures.name: mean gap
measures.historicalNote: all fifty states, every presidential cycle 1976-2016, from pres_state_panel.json and house_district_panel.json. Same definition both sides — the test program's SPEC one, top-of-ticket party's House share subtracted from 100. NOTE the source disagrees with itself: the worked table in the test program is keyed on the REPUBLICAN share in every row, which is a different quantity once the top of the ticket flips. On 1976 the two readings give 24.9pp and 75.1pp, and only the R-keyed one supports the table's "reversed" note.

measures.name: share of state-cycles above 69pp
measures.historicalNote: same population and same definition as the row above. For scale, the five Deep South states the test program tracks average 42.2pp over the same period — the extreme case the design is aimed at. There is no engine counterpart to that row, because the engine plays all fifty, so it is quoted here rather than measured.

measures.name: precondition: presidential-year state-cells with no House seat

items.verdict: mean gap 49.9pp against 39.0pp in the returns (all fifty states, 1976-2016); band 20-59pp. 46% of state-cycles clear 69pp against 14% historically; band 7-28%. The mean is inside the record and the tail is not: the board produces divergence of about the right average size and far too many extreme cases.

items.question: Does a district ever change its vehicle while keeping its interest?
items.verdict: 7% of consecutive holds change party against 6% changing interest — ratio 1.1 (target >=2). NOTE: candidate tag-fit is measured against the district a card actually ran in, so a district with no card in play contributes nothing.

items.question: Do concentration and diversity beat each other conditionally, or is the ladder perfectly transitive?
items.notRun: the duel matrix is `node sim/roundrobin.ts`, not re-run here. Acceptance: the matrix must NOT be perfectly transitive on both configs, and must include hand-written adversarial strategies designed to beat the top — if nothing in a reasonable strategy space beats it, that is structural. `WideAndEmpty` at 0.0% of every duel is the v0.1.2 reading.

items.question: Does the game have an ending, or only a timer?

measures.name: mean game length as a share of the cap

items.calibrated: the ending rate is downstream of amendment.dice/target/rescindTarget, which were swept -- but they are no longer swept to a number somebody liked. They are fitted to the postwar ratification rate, which D6 grades directly. So this item is calibrated in the sense that its value is a consequence of a fit, and the fit itself is the thing under test one item down.
items.verdict: 65% of games end by condition, against a 50-75% band derived from the record: ~1.2 amendments per 16 years postwar puts at least one in a 16-year window at 70% under Poisson, and the real series is bursty, which pushes the true figure below that. v0.1.2 was 0% on eight of nine configs.

items.question: Can a player behind at the midpoint still win?
items.verdict: determination at 63% against SIM-BRIEF's 75-85% band; comeback rate 6.7%

items.question: Do the failed impeachment, the shutdown and the shock move the board in the direction the record says?

measures.name: item 8: lean mass with shutdown blame
item 8: lean mass without shutdown blame

items.verdict: item 7 backfire fires; item 8 shutdown blame fires; item 9 shock moves determination by 0.0pp — i.e. NOT AT ALL, which is the branch the build order names: at 400 seeds on tuned.json the determination point is 0.625 with the shock and 0.625 without it. A shock proportional to power held is not a brake, so the brake has to be POSITIONAL — shocks discredit positions, stagflation discredited demand management, 2008 discredited deregulation — and the complexity of that version has now been earned rather than assumed. v0.3. NOTE: determination quantises to 1/maxYears, so a block below ~200 seeds cannot resolve this.

items.question: Do bills actually come off the books, or is the corpus monotone in a second costume?

measures.name: games whose bills had more than one author

items.verdict: 2% of games see a repeal (target >=20%), against 2% whose bills had more than one author. The rule is built and fires; what is missing is turnover in the pen — §12 hands authorship to the largest bloc of the majority House party and a faction holds both parties, so it never changes hands. Fix authorship, not repeal.

items.question: Does the president's party lose ground at the midterm, as it did in every postwar cycle but two?

measures.name: president's party loses seat share at the midterm
measures.historicalNote: 9 of 11 midterms 1978-2018 in house_district_panel.json; the two exceptions the data finds are 1998 and 2002, which are the two the record names. Same quantity both sides: share of House seats held by the president's party, against the previous election.

measures.name: historical band, lower (Wilson 95% on the record)
historical band, upper (Wilson 95% on the record)

items.verdict: 50% of midterms cost the president's party ground, against 81.8% in the returns (9 of 11, 1978-2018, the exceptions being 1998 and 2002). Band is the Wilson 95% interval on that: 52-95%. Derived from house_district_panel.json, not chosen.

items.question: Does the side that tries and fails to remove a president pay for it?
items.verdict: impeaching pool holds 46.6% of the board with the rule on against 49.0% with it off — the attempt must cost, not pay

items.question: Is the blame for a failed bill attached to the obstructor rather than to whoever happens to be out of power?

measures.name: blamed party held a chamber majority

items.verdict: the blamed party held a chamber majority in 80% of shutdowns. In 1995 and 2013 the blamed party held the congressional majority, so a rule that never blames the majority has encoded incumbency by accident. Target >20%.

items.question: Can a game even be long enough to contain one Skowronekian regime?
items.verdict: the cap is 16 years against a 30-40 year reference regime; below 30 a null settlement result is a fact about the clock

items.question: How long does the board take to turn lean into seats?

measures.name: median years from lean crossing to delegation flip
measures.historicalNote: the Deep South turned at the top of the ticket in 1964 and its House delegation went majority-R in 1996, per house_district_panel.json — a 32-year lag. The lean date is documented rather than derived: the panel starts in 1976 and the turn is outside it. NOT like-for-like on the clock: a game is 16 years, so a 32-year lag cannot occur in one, and the engine figure is bounded by the cap rather than by the rules.

measures.name: lean crossings that reached a delegation flip
Deep South R House share, first panel year
Deep South R House share, last panel year

items.verdict: median lag 0 years against 32 in the record (1964 lean -> 1996 delegation). The bar is >=8 years, a quarter of the historical figure, because a 16-year cap cannot contain 32 and grading against the full figure would grade the clock. See D4.

items.question: Does an amendment that reaches the states ratify as often as the real ones did?
items.calibrated: amendment.dice, target and rescindTarget were swept to land this on the postwar figure, on tuned.json specifically. That makes the tuned number a fit rather than a prediction; the OTHER configs are the out-of-sample test, and they are reported below rather than tuned to match.
items.verdict: 65% of proposals ratify, against 71% postwar (5 of 7 sent to the states after 1947) and 82% all-time (27 of 33). Band is 60-90%, which spans both point estimates and leaves room for the small-n uncertainty in 5 of 7. The convention-call rate alongside it has NO bar: Article V conventions have never been called, so the historical value is zero and the game needs an ending.
